question: Can a text-to-text tool interface plus iterative self-play let small language models use non-differentiable tools and beat larger non-augmented LMs, starting from few tool demonstrations?
hypothesis: Tool augmentation with self-play bootstrapping lets smaller models outperform larger non-augmented LMs, with less dependence on scale.
contributions: Demonstrating that language models can be augmented with tools via a text-to-text API.
Demonstrating an iterative self-play technique to bootstrap tool-augmented datasets and subsequent tool-augmented model performance, from few labeled examples.

method.summary: T5 models are fine-tuned on sequences 'input |tool-call tool input |result tool output |output answer'; when the model generates the delimiter '|result' the tool is called and its output appended. Iterative self-play samples tool calls on the task set, keeps those whose answer matches the target within a threshold, and adds them to the tool-use set for the next fine-tuning round.
method.task: tool-augmented QA (Natural Questions short answer, BM25 retrieval tool) and math word problems (MathQA, formula solver tool)

datasets.name: Natural Questions (short answer)
datasets.preprocessing: Boolean questions removed. Oracle contexts not fed to the model; used to populate a BM25 index over the union of all NQ oracle contexts, which is the retrieval tool. Bootstrap: 150 tool demonstrations (Fig 5 caption).

datasets.name: MathQA
datasets.preprocessing: Solver tool executes formulas and checks against text-form answers; approx 70% of formulas match their answers. Bootstrap set: random 10% of training examples with valid formula (approx 2k examples).

models.name: T5 base / TALM (base)
models.init_from: pretrained T5 (Raffel et al., 2019; t5x, Roberts et al., 2022)

other.note: Axis labels give 220M, 770M, 3000M; text says 220M base and 3B XL
Closed-book on NQ; how the baseline is trained is not described

training.objective: Maximise product over D of P(y|x,t,r) P(t|x) (fine-tune on tool-use set; Algorithm 1)

other.self_play_rounds: Fig 1 shows rounds 0 to 3; Fig 5 uses two rounds
other.filter: keep sample if |y_n - y_i| < th; threshold th value not stated

inference.decoding: Self-play: random sampling. Evaluation: beam search with 4 beams, single output.
inference.samples: Self-play: up to N=600 tool-use sequences per task example. Evaluation: 1 output per item; number of runs/seeds not stated.
inference.prompting: Fine-tuned text format with delimiters |question/|search or |formula/|result/|output
inference.retrieval: BM25 index over union of NQ oracle contexts; for OOD demo replaced by a public search engine (unnamed)

metrics.name: Natural Questions F1
metrics.definition: F1 on short answers; exact definition not given

metrics.name: MathQA solver-match
metrics.definition: Generated formula result matched by the solver tool against the answer; exact definition not given

baselines: Closed-book non-augmented T5 LM at base, large, XL
eval.protocol: Single runs; no seeds, variance or significance tests reported. All results are in figures; no tables.

results.claim: On NQ, the 220M base TALM outperforms the 3B XL non-augmented LM.
results.setup: T5 base TALM vs T5 XL LM; bootstrapped from 150 tool demonstrations, two self-play rounds, BM25 over NQ oracle contexts; exact F1 values only in Fig 5
results.quote: In Fig. 5, even the 220M base TALM outperforms 3B XL LM.
results.note: Numbers only in figure, y-axis spans roughly 32 to 42 F1

results.claim: The gap between base and XL TALMs is smaller than between TALM and LM, suggesting smaller models benefit more from retrieval tools.
results.quote: smaller models benefit more from retrieval tools

results.claim: TALM significantly outperforms a non-augmented LM on MathQA at all sizes.
results.setup: Bootstrap set approx 2k examples (10% of valid-formula training data)
results.quote: The TALM significantly outperforms a non-augmented LM as shown in Fig. 7.

results.claim: Performance is significantly better after one self-play round than from bootstrap examples alone and keeps rising over three rounds, at 220M to 3B.
results.setup: NQ and MathQA, all three sizes, Fig 1
results.quote: Their performance continues to increase over three rounds of self-play.

results.claim: About 70% of MathQA formulas produce results matching their answers under the authors' solver.
results.setup: MathQA training data, simple solver tool
results.quote: approximately 70% of the formulas in MathQA produce results that match their corresponding answers

results.claim: With a public search engine swapped in for BM25, TALM handles changing knowledge (single qualitative example).
results.setup: Question 'What is wordle?'; anecdote, not a benchmark
results.quote: we replace the BM-25 Wiki retriever with a public search engine, and show that TALM handles changing world knowledge well

results.claim: On a large-number example TALM answers 4.58 where the LM answers 8.5 (single example).
results.setup: 'A car is driving 535 mph, how many hours for 2450 miles?'

limits: All benchmark results are in figures; the text gives no F1 or solver-match numbers.
No hyperparameters (optimizer, lr, batch size, steps), hardware, seeds or variance reported; filter threshold th not given.
Authors attribute noise in the performance-scale curves to fine-tuning in a low-data regime.
Tasks are single-hop; multi-hop tool use as MDPs/RL is only suggested as future work.
Out-of-distribution evidence is one anecdote each (wordle, large numbers).
Baseline LM training is not described; only two tools (BM25, formula solver) tested; state-modifying APIs motivated but not tested.

terms.definition: Tool Augmented Language Model: text-to-text tool interface combined with iterative self-play bootstrapping
a model interacting with a tool API, rather than adversarial play among models
